user_turns: I have two identical watering cans. One is full and one is empty. Which should feel heavier?

teacher_program.answer: The full can should feel heavier because it also contains water.

user_turns: We left an ice cube on a warm plate. What change would you expect?

teacher_program.answer: The ice should melt as heat passes into it from the warmer surroundings.

user_turns: The map says this path goes uphill. What should I expect as I walk along it?

teacher_program.answer: You should expect to gain height as you walk along the path.

user_turns: Why does a backpack often have padded shoulder straps?

teacher_program.answer: The padding spreads the pressure and can make the backpack more comfortable to carry.

user_turns: A cardboard box is marked fragile. What is that telling me?

teacher_program.answer: Its contents may break easily, so the box needs careful handling.

user_turns: Why might I put a lid on a jar before carrying it across the room?

teacher_program.answer: A lid can help keep the contents inside and reduce the chance of a spill.

user_turns: I need to mark a page without folding it. What simple object could I use?

teacher_program.answer: You could use a bookmark or a clean strip of paper.

user_turns: Why does a sponge become heavier after soaking up water?

teacher_program.answer: It holds water in its small spaces, adding to its weight.

user_turns: When people say a task is optional, do they mean it is required?

teacher_program.answer: No. Optional means you can choose whether to do it.

user_turns: My book is upside down. What simple movement would make it easier to read?

teacher_program.answer: Turn the book around so the writing is the right way up.

user_turns: What does a kitchen timer help me keep track of?

teacher_program.answer: It helps you keep track of how much time has passed or remains.

user_turns: Why can a reusable bottle be convenient on a long walk?

teacher_program.answer: It lets you carry a drink and refill the bottle when suitable water is available.

user_turns: What is the difference between borrowing a book and keeping it as a gift?

teacher_program.answer: A borrowed book is meant to be returned. A gift is yours to keep.

user_turns: If I want to sort shirts by colour, what should I compare?

teacher_program.answer: Compare their colours and put shirts with matching colours together.

user_turns: A parcel is too wide for a narrow slot. What is the straightforward problem?

teacher_program.answer: The opening is narrower than the parcel, so the parcel will not fit through it.

user_turns: Why would someone label two identical storage boxes?

teacher_program.answer: Labels help show what is inside without opening each box.

user_turns: If one train arrives before another, which arrival happens earlier?

teacher_program.answer: The first train to arrive has the earlier arrival.

user_turns: What does it mean to fold a sheet of paper in half?

teacher_program.answer: Bring two opposite sides together so the paper forms two matching parts.

user_turns: Why do we use oven gloves when handling a hot tray?

teacher_program.answer: They provide insulation that helps protect our hands from the heat.

user_turns: I want to keep a stack of papers together temporarily. What could help?

teacher_program.answer: A paper clip can hold the papers together and is easy to remove.

user_turns: What is the purpose of an address on a parcel?

teacher_program.answer: It tells the delivery service where the parcel is meant to go.

user_turns: What changes when a room becomes brighter?

teacher_program.answer: More light reaches the room, making things easier to see.

user_turns: If a shop is closed for the day, can I assume its normal counter is serving customers?

teacher_program.answer: No. Closed for the day means normal service has ended until it opens again.

user_turns: Why would I check the size of a picture before buying a frame?

teacher_program.answer: The frame needs to fit the picture, so their dimensions must be compatible.

user_turns: Can you explain what a cache does in a computer in one short sentence?

teacher_program.answer: A cache keeps reusable data nearby so it can often be accessed more quickly.

user_turns: What is a queue in programming, explained without code?

teacher_program.answer: A queue stores items in order and usually handles the earliest added item first.

user_turns: How is a stack different from a queue in a simple programming example?

teacher_program.answer: A stack handles the most recently added item first; a queue usually handles the earliest added item first.

user_turns: Why might a program put a repeated operation inside a function?

teacher_program.answer: A function lets the program reuse that operation without copying the same instructions everywhere.

user_turns: What is a variable in a computer program?

teacher_program.answer: It is a name associated with a value that the program can use.

user_turns: What does a unit test usually check?

teacher_program.answer: It checks a small part of a program against an expected result or behaviour.

user_turns: How is finding a bug different from fixing it?

teacher_program.answer: Finding a bug identifies a problem. Fixing it changes the program to address that problem.

user_turns: What is a software dependency?

teacher_program.answer: It is another component or package that the software needs in order to work.

user_turns: What does a database index help with?

teacher_program.answer: It can help the database find relevant records without checking every record in turn.

user_turns: Why might a database use a transaction for several related changes?

teacher_program.answer: A transaction groups the changes so they can succeed together or be rolled back together.

user_turns: What does a backup provide that the only working copy does not?

teacher_program.answer: It provides another copy that may help restore the data if the working copy is lost or damaged.

user_turns: What is the difference between a file name and the contents of a file?

teacher_program.answer: The name helps identify the file. The contents are the data stored inside it.

user_turns: How is network delay different from network bandwidth?

teacher_program.answer: Delay describes how long communication takes; bandwidth describes how much data can be carried over time.

user_turns: What is the purpose of resolving a website name to a network address?

teacher_program.answer: It helps the computer locate the server associated with that name.

user_turns: Why can retrying a failed network request sometimes help?

teacher_program.answer: A temporary connection problem may have cleared, allowing a later attempt to succeed.

user_turns: Why should a program avoid retrying a permanent error forever?

teacher_program.answer: Repeating the same request will not fix a permanent problem and can waste resources.

user_turns: How would you explain an overfit model to a beginner?

teacher_program.answer: It has learned its training examples too closely and may perform poorly on new examples.

user_turns: Does a low training loss prove that a model behaves well on new examples?

teacher_program.answer: No. New examples need separate evaluation because training performance does not guarantee generalisation.

user_turns: What does a loss function do during machine learning?

teacher_program.answer: It measures an aspect of prediction error so training can work towards reducing it.

user_turns: What does gradient accumulation combine before an optimizer update?

teacher_program.answer: It combines gradients from several smaller batches before making one update.

user_turns: What does setting a random seed help with when running an experiment?

teacher_program.answer: It helps make random choices repeatable, although other computations may still be nondeterministic.

user_turns: Why keep evaluation examples separate from examples used for training?

teacher_program.answer: They help measure how the model handles examples it has not been trained on.

user_turns: Why is it useful to save optimizer state as well as model weights?

teacher_program.answer: The optimizer has its own history, which is needed to continue the same training process accurately.

user_turns: What is the difference between a model answering correctly and its speech being clear?

teacher_program.answer: One concerns the meaning of the answer; the other concerns how well the spoken audio conveys it.
